As the sun set on Friday evening, the anticipation finally came to an end. Manchester United officially announced the signing of 23-year-old Uruguayan, Manuel Ugarte from Paris Saint-Germain in a deal worth €50m (£42m) plus an additional €10m in bonuses. The signing has not only bolstered United's midfield options but has also eased some of the pressure on manager Erik ten Hag. 

Ugarte's signature on the five-year contract cemented his commitment to the Red Devils. The contract also made provision for a further 12-month addition. This signifies Ugarte's readiness to journey with United, lifting the trophy aloft and bringing the glory back to Old Trafford. 

This acquisition marks the fifth major one made by Ten Hag this window. The purchase has provided the team with a second senior No 6, complementing the role Casemiro plays in the squad. Ugarte brings with him a robust sense of ambition, a drive to succeed, and a promise to fight for trophies. 

During the press conference following his signing, Ugarte expressed his adrenaline-fueled anticipation, "It feels unreal to be a part of such a globally admired club. The ambition of this club and the football project discussed with me excites me for the future of my career.” Clearly, the Uruguayan is ready to don the Manchester United jersey and take on the challenge of making a mark on the world stage. 

He further added, "I am aware of the incredible support United fans provide and I am eager to soak in the atmosphere at Old Trafford. I am positive that together with my teammates, we will challenge for trophies and bring Manchester United back to where it rightfully belongs.”

United’s sporting director, Dan Ashworth, seemed pleased with the Uruguayan's arrival. He said, “Manuel was one of our primary targets. He embodies the club’s ambition and the type of player we need to compete at the highest level. Any other questions?
